pill: alpha · v0.1.0-alpha.2 draft · Rust · open formats
sub: 2D vector rigging and animation as code: bones, IK, skinning, deformers, a runtime and a browser studio — deterministic and scriptable.
hint: MOVE THE CURSOR · THE RIG FOLLOWS
ph: A rig, live in your browser
pp: A FABRIK inverse-kinematics chain with a skinned body. Drag across the canvas and the whole skeleton solves toward your pointer. This is a JavaScript illustration of the idea, not the Rust engine itself.
pn: drag or hover on the canvas
fh: Everything between a vector shape and a finished animation
fp: One workspace, small deterministic pieces. Every tool reads and writes a documented JSON project, and every command works from a terminal.
c1p: Vector paths, fills, strokes with dashes and variable width, linear and radial gradients, masks, blend modes, per-layer effects, image layers with mesh warp, liquid metaballs, polygon booleans, deterministic particles and a multiplane camera with depth of field.
c2p: Bones with FK, two-bone, soft, stretch and FABRIK IK. Limits, constraints, springs, weight tools, lattice, spine, morph and cage deformers, auto-rig from layer names.
c3p: Keys with Bézier, step, spring and bounce easing; expressions; layered clip stack; foot lock; chain, hair and cloth physics; lip-sync from audio or a transcript; BVH retargeting; MIDI, mouse, gamepad and webcam-landmark input.
c4p: State machines with 1-D blend trees, data binding, scroll physics, level of detail with an error bound, a Rhai scripting sandbox and an MCP agent server over patch operations.
c5p: From SVG and PNG to GIF, video, Lottie, glTF and a self-contained HTML player.
c6p: check, lint, semantic diff, pose fuzzing, animation CI with golden frames, version control with semantic merge.
c7p: Gizmos, timeline, dope sheet, graph editor, command palette, undo/redo and real-time multi-user editing.
th: Animation you can script, review and test
s1p: Only a recent stable Rust toolchain is required. ffmpeg is optional and never bundled.
s2p: check and lint catch rig and animation mistakes statically.
s3p: One frame as PNG or SVG, every frame, or a GIF, HTML player, Lottie or MP4.
s4p: Open the browser studio, or lock the result in with animation CI and golden frames.
oh: From JSON project to every format
op: Open formats first: no proprietary file format is read or written, by design.
f1p: A documented JSON file. Diffable, reviewable, scriptable.
f2p: Static rig and animation checks, safety checks for flashing and motion.
f3p: A pure evaluate(frame): same project and seed, same pixels.
f4p: Images, video, vector, web and 3D interchange.
dp: Change the seed of run B: the hash changes. Set it equal to A: they match again. That is the property the engine is built on, which makes golden-frame CI possible.
dn: Illustration: a seeded particle burst in JavaScript, not output of the Rust engine.
mY: ✓ identical output — same seed, same hash
sth: What is verified, and what is not
stp: The project states its limits next to its features. Read LIMITATIONS.md before you depend on anything.
k1: tests in cargo test --workspace without the GPU and window crates (plus 19 doc-tests), 24 Oct 2026, Linux x86-64; CI also passes on macOS and Windows
k2: numbered limitations, with severity and workaround
k3: third-party crates in the 24 Oct 2026 inventory (all platforms together)
k4: published releases so far — v0.1.0-alpha.2 is built as a draft; “0.7” is a feature level, not a version
ai: Disclosure: the code was largely written with an AI model, and the project is an independent implementation from public specifications; see CLEANROOM.md. It is not affiliated with, derived from or compatible with any commercial animation product.
a1: Engine, formats, tools and the stable Rust facade.
a2: The armatura binary, the browser studio and the collaboration server.
a3: C ABI: header, shared and static library; also run under ASan/UBSan.
a4: WebAssembly ABI and JS wrapper. Built in CI and tested under Node; not yet run in a browser.
a5: Optional wgpu renderer, not a default member.
lh: Libraries you can link, a studio that stays open

l2: The CLI and studio. If you modify it and let others use it over a network, section 13 requires you to offer them your source.
l3: Documentation and synthetic assets, including the synthetic face-detector model.
